name: kb_bible_commit
description: Commit one round of confirmed entries to the bible: { ids, baseBranch, baseCommit }. Merges exactly the given ids from this repository's KB into <repo>/.fleet/kb-canonical.json at ENTRY level -- only the given ids are added or replaced; every entry already in the file is kept unless this KB holds it as superseded or invalidated, and an entry in the file but not in the KB (or CONFIRMED and current, or merely stale) is never dropped -- in kb_export's stable serialization (v3 envelope, id order, ASCII-safe; each merged entry carries its stored source_file_hashes basis). provenance.branch is baseBranch (the sprint's target base branch) and provenance.commit is baseCommit (the base commit the entries were verified against), never the working folder HEAD. Then makes a local commit scoped to that one path (identity pm-kb). It NEVER pushes. Re-running with the same ids after resetting to a newer HEAD re-merges at entry level, so a rejected push can be retried with no manual merge. Ids that are unknown, stale, superseded, or not CONFIRMED are SKIPPED (never an error) and reported in skipped with reason not_confirmed_or_unknown. A CONFIRMED id is admitted only if it passes the same basis rule kb_export (scope=project) applies: every cited source file has a recorded per-file hash that matches that file's content at the repo's HEAD commit (an empty or missing basis, a cited file with no basis key, a file absent or changed at HEAD, or a path that is not repo-relative excludes it; uncommitted edits never change the verdict; a folder that is not a git work tree is refused, never hashed from disk); such an id is SKIPPED with reason basis_mismatch, logged, and any entry already in the bible for it is left unchanged. A CONFIRMED id that cites no source file has no checkable basis and is SKIPPED with its own reason no_source_files (never basis_mismatch), also leaving any existing bible entry unchanged. At every call (also with no ids) each bible entry this KB holds as superseded or invalidated is REMOVED and reported in removed as {id, reason} (reason superseded or invalidated); the commit message lists each removal. kb_export never removes entries. Also at every call, each bible entry with no source_file_hashes (carried over from a v1/v2 bible) that this KB holds under the same id, citing the same source files, with a stored basis that passes the same basis rule at HEAD gains that stored basis as its source_file_hashes (only that field changes; an entry that does not qualify is kept unchanged, never dropped); backfilled reports how many, and the commit message names the count. Nothing merged, nothing removed and nothing backfilled, or an unchanged entry set: no write and no commit. Refuses (throws, file untouched) when the existing bible file is unreadable or holds a duplicate id, or when the local commit fails. Under an http KB provider the call is skipped with bible_skipped:true and a reason, never an error (the KB is not read and nothing is written or committed). Returns {path, merged, skipped, removed, entry_count, backfilled, committed}. Scope: always the calling session's own KB -- a member session uses its registered work folder, any other session the fleet server's working folder; there is no repo/path scope argument (the removed repo_path, repo and repo_remote_url keys fail with E-SCOPE-KEY-REMOVED). Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER, E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO or E-SELF-NO-REMOTE (each with a one-line remediation) when that folder cannot carry a KB identity (it must be a git repository with an origin remote).
